title: What a PLC is: your first rung
summary: Meet the three parts of every PLC machine, inputs, a program and outputs, and finish a one-rung program that lights a lamp while a button is pressed.
scope: Tests provide deterministic native POSIX host evidence on your computer only; they are not hardware, electrical, HIL, or safety evidence.
objectives: Name the three parts of a PLC system: inputs that read the world, a program that decides, and outputs that act on the world.
Complete a Ladder rung in which a pressed button lights a lamp, and read the result in the simulated lab.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/WhatIsPlc.ld.json one rung is drawn: a coil named Lamp on the right. The coil is the output, the lamp. Add a normally open contact named StartButton on the left of the coil. The contact is the input, the button. Together they say: the lamp is lit while the button is pressed.
stages.checkpoint: The rung has a StartButton contact on its left and the Lamp coil on its right.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before you run anything, predict Lamp. The scenario presses the button at {{t:10}} ms and releases it at {{t:30}} ms. Is the lamp lit at {{t:20}} ms? At {{t:50}} ms?
stages.checkpoint: {{v:WhatIsPlc.Lamp=true@20|Lamp ON}} at {{t:20}} ms, because the button is held; {{v:WhatIsPlc.Lamp=false@50|lamp OFF}} at {{t:50}} ms, because it was released at {{t:30}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Fix this starter omission, save it, then press Check: The starter has the Lamp coil but nothing that reads the button, so power always reaches the coil and the lamp is lit at {{t:0}} ms before anyone presses anything. Add a normally open contact on StartButton to the left of the coil.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program in the simulated lab on this computer and compares what it did with the scenario of this lesson.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named WhatIsPlc and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: In the results, green means ON or TRUE and grey means OFF or FALSE. Red means something went wrong, such as a failed assertion. Compare {{t:0}}, {{t:10}} and {{t:30}} ms: the lamp turns green when the button turns green and grey when it is released.
stages.checkpoint: Lamp rises once at {{t:10}} ms and falls once at {{t:30}} ms, exactly with the button.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Which part is the input, which is the program and which is the output? Now think of a wall light switch: what would you call the switch, the wiring decision and the lamp?
stages.checkpoint: The scenario covers one button and one lamp in simulation. It does not show real wiring, hardware timing, or a safety function.

hints.text: The coil only lights when power reaches it from the left. What would you put in the path so that the button decides whether power reaches the coil?
Add a normally open contact to the left of the Lamp coil and give it the variable StartButton. Do not change the coil.

faultCases: The starter has the Lamp coil but nothing that reads the button, so power always reaches the coil and the lamp is lit at {{t:0}} ms before anyone presses anything; add a normally open contact on StartButton to the left of the coil.
